trans-unit.source: Some installed extensions can be enabled in the Agents window.

Extensions listed under AI Features haven't declared support for the Agents window but add AI features, such as tools, MCP servers, or skills, which are read as part of the extension. Like other extensions, they are disabled by default.

Extensions that add AI features and don't rely on views, debugging, or other features that are unavailable in the Agents window are enabled automatically instead. You can disable them like any other extension.
Some extensions that haven't declared support for the Agents window are enabled automatically instead. You can disable them like any other extension.

Extensions that support the Agents window are listed under Supported and are enabled by default. Other extensions are listed under Other Extensions and are disabled by default because they might not work as expected.

Use the search box to filter extensions by name, identifier, publisher, or description. Press Tab to move to the list, use the Up and Down Arrow keys to move between extensions, and press Space or Enter to enable or disable the focused extension. Use the Left and Right Arrow keys on a group to collapse or expand it.

You are in the Extensions section of Agent Customizations. It lists the extensions installed in VS Code and whether each one runs in the Agents window. Enabling or disabling an extension here only affects the Agents window.

When a change requires restarting extensions or reloading the window, the extension is marked as requiring a restart, and a Restart Extensions or Reload Window button appears on its row and next to the section title. Press Shift+Tab from the search box to reach the button next to the section title.

Extensions that haven't declared support for the Agents window and contribute views, debuggers, status bar items, or walkthroughs, which are not supported in the Agents window, have a warning, which is read as part of the extension.
Extensions that add AI features, such as tools, MCP servers, or skills. They haven't declared support for the Agents window, so they are disabled by default and might not work as expected.

Extensions that add AI features, such as tools, MCP servers, or skills. They haven't declared support for the Agents window, so they might not work as expected. Those that don't rely on views, debugging, or other features that are unavailable in the Agents window are enabled automatically.

Extensions that add AI features, such as tools, MCP servers, or skills. They haven't declared support for the Agents window, so they might not work as expected. They are disabled by default, unless they are enabled automatically.

Choose which installed extensions run in the Agents window. Extensions that haven't declared support for the Agents window are disabled by default and might not work as expected. Changes only apply to the Agents window.

Choose which installed extensions run in the Agents window. Extensions that haven't declared support for the Agents window might not work as expected. They are disabled by default, unless they could be useful there and don't rely on features that are unavailable in the Agents window. Changes only apply to the Agents window.

Choose which installed extensions run in the Agents window. Extensions that haven't declared support for the Agents window might not work as expected. They are disabled by default, unless they are enabled automatically. Changes only apply to the Agents window.
Extensions you install in VS Code appear here.
Contributes {0}, which are not supported in the Agents window.
Extensions that haven't declared support for the Agents window. They are disabled by default and might not work as expected.

Extensions that haven't declared support for the Agents window. They might not work as expected. Those that add AI features and don't rely on views, debugging, or other features that are unavailable in the Agents window are enabled automatically. The others are disabled by default.
Extensions that haven't declared support for the Agents window. They might not work as expected. They are disabled by default, unless they are enabled automatically.

Extensions that support the Agents window. They are enabled by default.

Choose which installed extensions run in the Agents window.

Controls which installed extensions that haven't declared support for the Agents window are enabled there automatically. When `true`, extensions that add AI features, such as tools, MCP servers, or skills, and don't rely on views, debugging, or other features that are unavailable in the Agents window are enabled. When set to a list of extension identifiers, such as `publisher.name`, only the listed extensions are enabled, even if they rely on features that are unavailable in the Agents window. You can still disable them from the Extensions section of Agent Customizations. Requires `#{0}#`.
Expected an extension identifier in the format `publisher.name`.

When enabled, you can choose which installed extensions run in the Agents window from the Extensions section of Agent Customizations. When disabled, extensions that don't support the Agents window stay disabled there, and your previous choices are kept but ignored.

When enabled, the Agents window suggests installed extensions that add AI features, such as tools, MCP servers, or skills. The Extensions section of Agent Customizations lists them in an AI Features group, and its entry point shows a badge while they are disabled, until you open the section. Requires `#{0}#`.
When enabled, non-built-in extensions can declare whether they support running in the Agents window. Built-in extensions can declare support without enabling this setting.
